description: Apply value embeddings on every layer by making has_ve always return True.
Replace relu^2 MLP with SwiGLU at matched params (hidden 1344 ≈ 8/3*dim, gate and up fused in c_fc).
Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 so grad accumulation drops to 2 and more optimizer steps fit in the 300s budget.
Set Adam beta1 to 0.9 (from 0.8) for the AdamW parameter groups.
Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.3 so training spends more time at peak LR before decaying.
Clip gradient norm to 1.0 before the optimizer step.
Set HEAD_DIM to 64 so the model uses 12 heads at width 512 instead of 4 heads of dim 128.
Set DEPTH to 6 (model_dim 384, 3 heads) so the smaller model runs faster and sees more tokens in 300s.

issues: Nothing to flag on integrity. The diff changes one line, DEPTH 8 -> 6. It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines, the prepare.py import line or the evaluation call and summary printing.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. A shallower model gets more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s, so a better val_bpb is plausible. If model width is derived from DEPTH (an aspect-ratio setting), the model also gets narrower. That is a legitimate change, but it means 'DEPTH 6' changes the model size more than the one line suggests.

Statistical caveat: the incumbent mean comes from only 1 run, so the numbers give no estimate of the incumbent's run-to-run variance. The two candidate runs (1.0651, 1.0652) have a sample SD of about 7e-5. That is far smaller than any z=4.291 noise scale and should not be used as the noise estimate.

I could not recompute z from the numbers given. The mean difference is 1.0929 - 1.06515 = 0.02775. The reported z=4.291 implies a noise SD of about 0.00647, which must come from a prior the harness keeps elsewhere and is not shown. The size of the gain (~0.028 bpb) is large relative to typical seed noise, so the accept decision looks reasonable. A replicate of the incumbent would make the comparison sounder.

description: Set DEPTH to 6 (model_dim 384, 3 heads) so the smaller model runs faster and sees more tokens in 300s.
Remove per-step .item() and cuda synchronize; sync, NaN-check, time accounting and logging only every 10 steps (every step for the first 11) so the CPU can run ahead of the GPU.
Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the learning rate ramps up linearly over the first 2% of the time budget.
Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4 for the token and value embedding Adam groups.
Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**17 so each optimizer step is one 64x2048 micro-batch with no grad accumulation, giving many more steps in 300s.
Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.7 so the LR decays linearly over the last 70% of the time budget.
Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.1 (from 0.2) for Muon cautious weight decay.

issues: No integrity problems. The diff only adds torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) just before optimizer.step(). It does not touch the seed lines, the prepare.py import line, the data, the evaluation call or the final summary printing.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The clip sits after the gradients are computed and before step/zero_grad, so it is placed correctly. On Muon-managed matrices it does little, because Muon orthogonalizes the update and the gradient scale mostly drops out. So in practice it mainly affects the AdamW groups (embeddings, lm_head, scalars). It also adds a global-norm reduction every step, which costs a little throughput inside the fixed 300 s budget. That is a cost, not an error.

The claim matches the numbers. The candidate scored 1.0649 against an incumbent mean of 1.0652, a difference of 0.0003 in the right direction (lower is better). With z = 0.034 that is far inside the noise, so the provisional reject holds.

I can't recompute z independently. The harness gave only the incumbent mean, not the two individual run values or their spread, and there is a single candidate run. The reported z = 0.034 implies a noise scale of about 0.0088 bpb (0.0003 / 0.034). That would be large for this setup, so it is worth checking that the harness's variance estimate isn't inflated, for example by being based on just n=2 runs.
Simplicity: one line for a gain that can't be told apart from zero. Under the program card's simplicity rule it does not earn a place, and a replicate run is probably not worth a slot.

description: Clip gradient norm to 1.0 (no .item()) after the micro-step backward passes and before optimizer.step() on the DEPTH 6 base.
Set WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSSSL" so only the final layer uses full-context attention in the 6-layer model.
Abort: WEIGHT_DECAY 0.1 was already run in slot 14 (1.0651, -0.0001, within noise, rejected).
Set ADAM_BETAS to (0.8, 0.99) for a smoother second-moment estimate in the AdamW groups.
Ramp Muon momentum from 0.85 to 0.97 (instead of 0.95) over the first 300 steps.
Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05 for the Muon parameter groups.
